  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "r:5326086280",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Handle the no-timeout case using the OS primitives' native indefinite timeout (NULL for select, negative for poll) while keeping the cap for large finite timeouts",
      "quote": "could we handle the \"_no timeout_\" case using the OS primitives' native indefinite timeout, while keeping this cap for explicitly specified large finite timeouts ?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "accepted",
      "status_note": "author dropped the second commit to simplify backporting; winterrdog dropped the suggestion and gave Approach ACK",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5847188854",
        "c:5865812893"
      ],
      "other_replies": [
        "c:5865455142",
        "c:5865809869"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:5865945894",
      "status_by_quote": "A protracted wait timeout is simple and does the job fine. So, no need to get dogmatic about native infinite wait"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5865455142",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "scope",
      "text": "Limit the change to the first commit (or a smaller cap) to ease backporting",
      "quote": "I wonder how much we want to backport here. I doubt there is a use case to have a timeout of more than a few hours, so capping to 1 day, or even 14 days, or the first commit should be fine for a backport?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author dropped the second commit to keep the backport simple",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5865812893",
        "c:5872317032"
      ],
      "other_replies": [
        "c:5865809869"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5865812893",
      "status_by_quote": "dropped the second commit so this is just the cap in `Sock::WaitMany` and should be easy to backport."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4123034508",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Start Wait() in a thread and send data after a delay to ensure select()/poll() actually wait with the large timeout",
      "quote": "i am wondering if we should instead have `Wait()` start first, and then send a few bytes, so that we actually make `select()`/`poll()` wait with the large timeout.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author updated the unit test to wait in a thread before sending data",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5872317032"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5872317032",
      "status_by_quote": "the test now starts `Wait()` in a thread with the 5 year timeout and only sends the data after 100ms"
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "r:5326086280",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "",
      "substantive": false,
      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5865945894",
      "verdict": "Approach ACK",
      "reason": "A protracted wait timeout is simple and does the job fine. So, no need to get dogmatic about native infinite wait",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": []
    }
  ],
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "reviewer",
      "what": "winterrdog to review the updated test and comment changes",
      "id": "c:5872317032"
    }
  ],
  "notes": "kriss39 dropped the second commit to ease backporting as suggested by maflcko. winterrdog agreed, gave Approach ACK, and suggested updating the regression test to exercise the timeout asynchronously, which kriss39 implemented."
}
